Hours and seasons

You can visit any time of year. Some things close for the season, though, so check the list before you come.

Park
Open all year, 24 hours
Basin Lodge
Open all year
Cedar Flats Campground
May to October. Quiet hours 10 pm to 6 am.
Trails
Open all year. Expect snow above 7,500 ft most of the year.
Pass Hut
Staffed daily through Sept. 30. From November to May, Tomás patrols the pass on skis and keeps the hut stocked.
Rangers on duty
31 in summer, about a dozen in winter

Wildflowers in Halloran Meadows peak in July. The elk bulls bugle through September, and you can hear them from the lodge.

Fees and passes

One pass covers a vehicle and everyone in it. Hang it from your rearview mirror so a ranger can see it.

  • Vehicle pass

    $30

    Good for seven days. Sold at both entrance stations and online.

  • Cedar Flats campsite

    $28/night

    Per site. Book ahead for summer weekends.

  • Backcountry permit

    $12 per group

    Needed for overnight trips above Halloran Meadows. Pick it up in person at the ranger station.

Lodge rooms start at $189 a night and cabins at $240. See Lodging for what's included.

SAMPLE

Getting here

We're about two and a half hours from the city. There are two ways in, and each has an entrance station where you can buy a pass.

  • West Entrance

    At the west end of the lake, by the Echo River. Lakeshore Rd runs from here along the north shore to Basin Lodge, past the Cathedral Stand trailhead.

  • South Entrance

    On the south road through Cedar Gap, past the ranger station. The road meets Lakeshore Rd near Cedar Flats, and you follow that around the head of the lake to the lodge. Come this way if you need a backcountry permit.

Paper maps are free at both entrance stations. The nearest town is sixty miles away, so get gas before you leave the highway.

Accessibility

  • The Cathedral Stand boardwalk is flat and wheelchair accessible, with accessible parking at the trailhead. The rest of the 2.8 mile loop climbs 300 ft.
  • Basin Lodge has two accessible rooms with roll-in showers, both on the ground floor near the lobby. Ask for one when you book.
  • The dock is level with the path from the lodge, and staff can help you in and out of a canoe.
  • You can buy a pass and pick up a map at either entrance station without getting out of your car.

Common questions

Is the park open in winter?

Yes. The lodge stays open and we plow the road to it all winter. Cedar Flats closes for the season. Above Halloran Meadows you'll need skis or snowshoes, so check with a ranger before you go up.

Will my phone work?

Around the lodge, mostly. There's no cell coverage past it, so take a paper map and sign the trail register before you set out.

Can I have a campfire?

Yes, in the fire rings at Cedar Flats. Fire danger is moderate right now, so keep it small and put it all the way out before bed.

Can I swim in the lake?

You can, but it's cold even in August, and there's no lifeguard. It's 260 feet deep off the lodge dock.

Can I shout at Echo Point?

Everybody does. From the rail you'll hear four echoes, one for each cliff. June's echo talk at 10 and 2 explains why.
